subject: Discovery recap + proposed POC roadmap & streaming integration
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: James Park <james@oliveanalytics.com>
Cc: Lina Cho <lina@oliveanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + proposed POC roadmap & streaming integration

Hi James / Lina,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great conversation and very helpful to see how Olive Analytics is approaching real-time anomaly detection across your ingestion pipeline. Below is a concise recap, proposed success criteria, and a recommended 4-week POC roadmap we discussed. Please flag anything I missed or want to adjust.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: reduce false positives on alerts while preserving sub-200ms median inference latency for streaming inference.
- Data: batched historical logs + live Kafka topic (topic name TBD).
- Minimum viable integration: Redwood text-embedding + sequence-ranking + a lightweight reranker function called as a tool when model confidence is low.
- Constraints: PII in logs must remain in your VPC; only tokenized inputs to Redwood.

Proposed POC success criteria (quantitative + qualitative)
1) Latency: 95th percentile <= 400ms from Kafka event to model response in your staging region.
2) Accuracy lift: reduce false positive rate by >= 18% on the test set you provided.
3) Throughput: sustain 150 QPS with batching and prefix caching enabled.
4) Operational: end-to-end deploy with monitoring + alert on regressions; ability to roll back to baseline model within 15 minutes.

4-week POC roadmap (high level)
Week 0 (this week): finalize scope & sign off on allowed sample dataset + sandbox creds (you to provide).
Week 1: SDK integration + direct API routes for batch eval; ingest historical dataset; run baseline metrics.
Week 2: Streaming integration (Kafka connector + Redwood streaming SDK), implement tool-calling fallback for low-confidence cases.
Week 3: Load run, tuning (batching params / quantization profile), and build dashboards.
Week 4: Validation run, handoff, and decision meeting (go/no-go).

Ownership
- Redwood: Stephanie (sales lead) + Dylan (solutions engineer) — Dylan will be our primary technical contact for integration.
- Olive: James (PM) + Lina (engineering lead).

Attachments I shared: poc scope outline, sample schema that would help Dylan wire up the connector, and Redwood streaming SDK quickstart.

Requested next actions
1) James: share a 2–3 day retention sample (anonymized) + Kafka staging topic details and a sandbox user with read-only access.
2) Lina: confirm that tool-calling (external function execution) is allowed for the POC and whether it needs extra approval.
3) Olive: sign the attached short POC statement of work (we can iterate).

If this looks good I’ll spin up the initial sandbox and schedule a technical kickoff with Dylan for next Tuesday.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
redwood.ai
From: James Park <james@oliveanalytics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Cho <lina@oliveanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + proposed POC roadmap & streaming integration

Thanks Stephanie — this is helpful and aligns closely with our internal notes. A few small adjustments from our side: 

- Latency: our hard SLA for the staging evaluation is 500ms p95 (we can accept 400ms as a stretch goal).
- Throughput: current initial target is 120 QPS; we can scale to 150 QPS in week 3 if the connector behaves.
- Tool-calling: approved for POC but needs to run inside our VPC via a webhook (we will provide a signed TLS cert).

We can provide an anonymized 7-day sample by EOD Monday and will create a read-only sandbox user for your test cluster. I'll also attach the Kafka schema and topic naming conventions.

One ask: Lina would like to see an outline of the expected SDK footprint (memory/CPU) and recommended batch sizes so we can confirm instance sizing ahead of the technical kickoff.

If we can get the SOW this week, I’ll route it to procurement.

Appreciate the clear plan — looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
James
Head of Product, Olive Analytics
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, James Park <james@oliveanalytics.com>, Lina Cho <lina@oliveanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap + proposed POC roadmap & streaming integration

Dylan — looping you in to own the tech kickoff and the streaming connector work. Key asks from Olive:
- Validate p95 latency target: baseline 400ms stretch / 500ms acceptable.
- Provide SDK footprint guidance (memory/CPU) and recommended batch sizes for 120–150 QPS.
- Implement tool-calling via their VPC webhook; they will provide TLS cert and sandbox creds.

Attachments: 2026-05-30_poc_scope_outline.xlsx, sample_schema_example.json, redwood_streaming_sdk_quickstart.pdf

Proposed kickoff: Tuesday 2026-06-03 10:00 PT. Please confirm availability and any pre-kickoff items you need from Olive.

Thanks — Stephanie

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, James Park <james@oliveanalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lina Cho <lina@oliveanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery recap + proposed POC roadmap & streaming integration

Thanks — I’m on it. Quick technical notes and asks before the kickoff: 

1) SDK footprint (prelim)
- Typical sidecar: 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM for low-latency path with quantized models; recommend 4 vCPU, 12 GB RAM if you run multiple model variants.
- Batch sizes: start at 8–16 for 120 QPS, increase to 24–32 for 150 QPS during load tuning.

2) Streaming design
- We’ll use a lightweight Kafka consumer in your VPC that forwards tokenized payloads to Redwood via the streaming SDK.
- Implement prefix/KV caching on our end to reduce repeated tokenization cost.
- Tool-calling: I need the webhook endpoint + cert and a sample signed request to validate HMAC/TLS config.

3) Test data
- The sample_schema_example.json looks good; can you also provide one full example event (raw) with redaction notes so we can validate tokenization edge cases?

I’m available for the 2026-06-03 10:00 PT kickoff. I’ll bring a short checklist and a minimal test harness to run a 15-minute smoke test during the call.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
